# AetherFit AI

**Personalised fitness planning: ML-based fitness-level and injury-risk estimates, plus workout, nutrition and recovery plans generated by an agentic LangGraph workflow.**

A FastAPI backend serves a React single-page app. Plans are saved per browser, can be exported (PDF / calendar / JSON) and tracked over time, and can be re-planned from logged progress.

> ⚠️ **Educational tool, not medical advice.** The prediction models are trained on a bundled dataset whose statistics indicate it is synthetic. They have not been clinically validated. See [docs/MODEL_CARD.md](docs/MODEL_CARD.md).

## Features

- **Assessment** – free-text answers ("jogged 2 years, nothing since 2023", "45 min, 3×/week") are normalised, then two calibrated Random Forest models estimate **fitness level** and **injury risk**, with class probabilities and per-prediction driver explanations.
- **Safety guardrails** – rules (not the LLM) decide *standard / conservative / clinician-first*: they cap intensity and weekly sessions, floor calories and require clearance for red-flag input. The LLM cannot loosen them.
- **Plans** – weekly workout schedule, calorie/macro targets with Indian-cuisine meal ideas, and recovery / habit guidance.
- **Two generation modes** – *Simulated* (deterministic, input-aware, no key) and *Live* (Google Gemini, bring-your-own-key). Simulated output is always labelled as such.
- **Live progress** – the plan streams node-by-node over server-sent events.
- **Save, export, track** – plans are stored per device; export PDF, `.ics` calendar or JSON; log sessions and weigh-ins; **Re-plan** adjusts volume by adherence and inserts a deload when due.
- **Model transparency page** – live held-out evaluation, feature importance, guardrails and limitations.

```text
React SPA ──/api/v1──▶ FastAPI ──▶ services ──▶ LangGraph workflow
 (Vite, TS)             │  rate limit, CORS,        form_parser → input_normalizer → fitness_scorer
 SSE via fetch          │  request ids,             → injury_assessor → safety_guardrail
                        │  redacted logs            → workout_planner → nutrition_advisor → recovery_optimizer
                        ▼                                   │                    │
                    SQLite (plans,                    sklearn models        LLM client
                    progress logs)                    (artifacts/)     Gemini (BYOK) │ Mock
```

Every node is skipped once a fatal problem is recorded (invalid input, rejected API key, model failure). Non-fatal failures produce a **partial** plan with the failing section clearly reported, never fabricated defaults.

## Quick start

**Requirements:** Python 3.11+ (3.12 in Docker/CI), Node 22+.

```bash
make install          # backend deps (pip) + frontend deps (npm ci)
make dev-api          # http://localhost:8000  (docs at /api/docs)
make dev-web          # http://localhost:5173  (proxies /api to :8000)
```

Or the full stack in containers:

```bash
docker compose up --build     # http://localhost:8080
```

Open the app, fill in the form and generate a plan in *Simulated* mode – no key needed.

### Using Gemini (Live mode)

1. Get a key at [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey).
2. **Settings → Live (Gemini)** → paste it → *Save for this tab*.

Your key stays in that tab's `sessionStorage`, is sent only as the `X-Gemini-Api-Key` header, and is never stored, logged or echoed by the server.

## Project layout

```text
backend/
  app/
    api/v1/        routes (assessments, progress, system) + dependencies
    services/      assessment, progress, evaluation, export (PDF/ICS) services
    graph/         LangGraph state, nodes, workflow
    llm/           LLMClient interface, Gemini (retries/timeouts), Mock, prompts/*.md
    domain/        pure rules: BMI, safety, nutrition maths, free-text heuristics
    ml/            shared features, model registry (hash + version checks), predictors
    schemas/       Pydantic models (API contract + LLM output schemas)
    db/            SQLAlchemy models, repository (all queries device-scoped)
  ml_pipeline/     data cleaning, metrics, reproducible training (`make train`)
  artifacts/       trained models + metadata.json (metrics, versions, sha256)
  data/            bundled training / evaluation CSVs
  tests/           pytest suite (unit, graph, API, ML, export)
frontend/          React + Vite + TypeScript, plain CSS, vitest
docs/              MODEL_CARD.md, DEPLOYMENT.md
```

## Development

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| All tests | `make test` (pytest with coverage + vitest) |
| Lint & types | `make lint typecheck` |
| Everything CI runs | `make check` |
| Retrain models | `make train` (~25 s; rewrites `backend/artifacts/`) |
| Regenerate API types | `make openapi` (after changing backend schemas) |
| Live Gemini smoke test | `GEMINI_API_KEY=… pytest -m live` (opt-in; excluded by default) |

The frontend's TypeScript types are generated from the backend's OpenAPI schema (`frontend/openapi.json` → `src/api/schema.d.ts`); CI fails if they drift.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). The original review and roadmap are in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md).

## API

Interactive docs at `/api/docs`. Highlights (all under `/api/v1`, all need `X-Device-Id`):

| Method & path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /assessments` · `POST /assessments/stream` | create a plan (JSON or SSE progress) |
| `GET /assessments` · `GET/DELETE /assessments/{id}` | list / fetch / delete saved plans |
| `GET /assessments/{id}/export.{pdf,ics,json}` | exports |
| `GET/POST /assessments/{id}/logs` · `GET …/progress` | log sessions & weight; adherence summary |
| `POST /assessments/{id}/replan` (`/replan/stream`) | new plan from logged progress |
| `GET /models/info` · `GET /models/evaluation` | model metadata & held-out metrics |
| `GET /health` | liveness / readiness |

Errors are uniform: `{"error": {"code", "message", "field_errors", "request_id"}}`.

## Known limitations

- **Identity is anonymous and device-scoped** (a random id in `localStorage`). There are no accounts yet; clearing browser data loses access to saved plans.
- The models learn from synthetic data. Accuracy on the held-out CSVs (fitness 79 %, injury risk 69 %) says nothing about real-world validity. The injury model leans conservative on the evaluation set.
- The rate limiter is in-process (single worker). Use a shared limiter when scaling out.
- The database uses `create_all` (no migrations yet).
- The Live Gemini path is covered by mocked/fake-client tests; run the opt-in live test with your own key before relying on it.
